buy_title: The hand warmers to order after you check the recall list
buy_total: The button shows today's price; as an Amazon Associate we earn from qualifying purchases, and it never changes what you pay.

cards.name: THAW 2K Rechargeable Hand Warmer, 2-pack
cards.badge: Our pick · no CPSC recall found · US brand at big-box stores
cards.chip: 2,000 mAh each · up to 4 hours · 113°F max
cards.price: $24.99 at Target (read on Target's page, Nov 25, 2026); $29.99 list at THAW's own store. The button shows today's price.
cards.buy_if: you want one warmer per pocket from a US company sold at Target, Home Depot and Dick's, with a gentle 113°F top temperature and a one-year warranty at Target.
cards.skip_if: you need a full day of heat (THAW says up to 4 hours, and Target reviewers report less) or you use warmers only a few days a year (disposables are cheaper).
cards.owners: Target's 2-pack page showed 4.43 out of 5 from 26 reviews on Nov 25, 2026. The repeated complaint is runtime: one reviewer reports about an hour and a half (Nov 14, 2026), another about 3 hours (Jan 3, 2026). Others dislike one button for both light and heat.

buy.pick: THAW 2K Rechargeable Hand Warmer 2-pack (item THA-HND-0022), not a look-alike magnetic pair
buy.check: Brand THAW on the listing and the unit; sold by THAW or the store itself; 2,000 mAh, 113°F and USB-C in the specs
buy.label: See today's price

cards.name: Zippo HeatBank 9s Rechargeable Hand Warmer (Silver)
cards.badge: Longest runtime claim · no CPSC recall found · stock is thin
cards.price: $37.46–$44.96 on sale at zippo.com (list $49.95–$59.95, most colors sold out, Nov 25, 2026). The button shows today's price.
cards.buy_if: you spend long days outside (hunting, ski lifts, game days), want one unit that doubles as a phone power bank, and like a brand with a US support line.
cards.skip_if: you want two hands warm for under $30 (the THAW pair), or you expect the full 9 hours on a cold day: Bob Vila's freezer test got about 5.
cards.owners: Bob Vila's testers (Feb 19, 2026) liked the shape and fast warm-up but measured about 5 hours against the 9-hour claim. Older REI reviews in search snippets mention units that stopped charging (undated, unverified).
cards.video_title: Zippo HeatBank 9s Rechargeable Hand Warmer Review
cards.video_why: An owner's look at the 9s: the buttons, the heat levels and the size in a hand. We could not confirm the upload date.

buy.pick: Zippo HeatBank 9s, Silver (5,200 mAh), not the discontinued 9s Plus
buy.check: Sold by Zippo or the store itself; 'HeatBank 9s' and 5,200 mAh in the title; skip sites selling it far below Zippo's sale price
buy.label: See today's price

cards.name: THAW 5K Rechargeable Hand Warmer
cards.badge: Hotter and longer · same US brand · no CPSC recall found
cards.price: $39.99 at THAW's own store for the 5K+ (Nov 25, 2026); about $31–$35 at Walmart and Dick's in search snippets we could not open. The button shows today's price.
cards.buy_if: you want one stronger warmer with three heat levels and a one-year warranty, from the same company as our pick.
cards.skip_if: the warmer will sit against bare skin or go to a child or someone with numb hands: the original 5K reaches 140°F on high, well inside the burn range.
cards.owners: We found no dated owner reports outside Amazon for the 5K. A YouTube family review of a THAW warmer complains of short battery life and low heat (model not confirmed).

buy.pick: THAW 5K or 5K+ Rechargeable Hand Warmer (the 5K+ tops out at 120°F, the older 5K at 140°F)
buy.check: Brand THAW; 5,000 or 5,100 mAh; read which version the listing is before you buy
buy.label: See today's price

cards.name: HotHands Hand Warmers, air-activated (10-pair pack)
cards.badge: No battery · cheapest for a few cold days
cards.chip: Up to 10 hours · about 135°F · no charging
cards.price: $7.49 for 10 pairs at Target (Nov 25, 2026), about 75 cents a pair. The button shows today's price.
cards.buy_if: you need warm hands on a handful of days a season, for a car kit, a stadium or a kid's ski trip, and want nothing that charges.
cards.skip_if: you are out most cold days (a rechargeable pays for itself after about 33 pairs), or you dislike throwing a packet away every time.
cards.owners: Target's 10-pair page showed 4.81 out of 5 from 212 ratings on Nov 25, 2026. Expired packs can be duds: HotHands gives a shelf life of 3 to 4 years.

buy.pick: HotHands air-activated Hand Warmers, 10-pair or 40-pair pack (not the recalled rechargeable HotHands H163650)
buy.check: Air-activated packets, not an electric unit; a far-off expiration date on the box
buy.label: See today's price
